posts.title: Claro Switches On Liucura’s First 5G Site Ahead of Its 2027 Schedule
posts.description: Claro Chile switched on Liucura’s first 5G site on November 26, ahead of the operator’s planned 2027 delivery. Chile’s telecom regulator, Subtel, said it accepted the station after an on-site inspection that checked backup power, data transmission and emergency alert messaging. The site is in the Lonquimay municipality, about 17 kilometres from the Pino Hachado crossing on Chile’s border with Argentina. The station is part of Claro’s obligation to cover designated rural and border communities. Rodrigo Sahr, Claro Chile’s vice president for brand, communications and sustainability, said the operator was several months ahead of its projected schedule for Liucura and was working through the third and final stage of its 5G commitment to the state. posts.title: APCN-2 Is Set to Retire in December After 25 Years Linking Asian Networks
posts.description: The Asia Pacific Cable Network 2, a 19,000 km subsea fibre system that has linked eight Asian markets since 2001, is scheduled to retire in December 2026. Its consortium held its final management committee meeting on November 20 in Kuala Lumpur, according to a public update from Mohd Nazmi Abdul Rauf of Telekom Malaysia. The update gives the planned retirement month. It leaves the exact switch-off date and individual operators’ migration schedules open. The cable, known as APCN-2, began carrying commercial traffic on December 20, 2001. Its ring linked mainland China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Taiwan. NEC, the system supplier, says the original cable connected 10 landing stations. The companies behind it included carriers such as Telekom Malaysia, Singtel, KDDI, NTT Communications and PLDT, according to the launch announcement archived by Submarine Networks. posts.title: Viettel and Singtel Begin Building Subsea Cable With a New Late 2030 Target
posts.description: Viettel and Singtel have moved their Southeast Asian subsea cable project into construction, with the consortium now targeting completion in the fourth quarter of 2030. The Vietnam–Thailand–Singapore (VTS) consortium signed commercial and construction contracts with Japan’s NEC and Singapore’s ASEAN Cableship on November 26 in Ho Chi Minh City. The project is designed to span about 2,500 km and carry up to 600 Tbps across the system, according to Singtel’s announcement. The construction launch gives the project a more concrete schedule than the memorandum that started it. When TelecomTalk covered the April 2024 Viettel and Singtel agreement , the timeline pointed to the second quarter of 2027 for the system to go into operation. The new announcement puts the construction completion target in late 2030.
